STIPULATED DAMAGES SCHEDULE — FINAL EXECUTED COPY

Meridian Fabrication Corp. v. Corvess Industrial Group, LLC, No. 24-cv-8812 (D. Ariz.)

This Stipulated Damages Schedule (the "Schedule") is entered into by Plaintiff Meridian Fabrication Corp. ("Meridian") and Defendant Corvess Industrial Group, LLC ("Corvess") solely to narrow the issues for trial. This Final Executed Copy supersedes in its entirety the circulated draft designated v1, which shall have no evidentiary or computational effect.

Section 1. Definitions.
1.1 "Breach Date" means November 1, 2023, the date Corvess ceased performance under the Master Supply Agreement.
1.2 "Lost Profits" means the profits Meridian would have earned on the terminated purchase orders, as stipulated in Section 2.
1.3 "Consequential Carve-Out" means the categories of consequential damages identified in Section 5, which are excluded from Lost Profits and tracked separately on the docket.

Section 2. Stipulated Lost Profits.
2.1 The parties stipulate that Meridian's Lost Profits are fixed at exactly $1,840,000 (one million eight hundred forty thousand dollars). No further proof of the amount of Lost Profits shall be required at trial.

Section 3. Prejudgment Interest on Lost Profits.
3.1 Prejudgment interest on the Lost Profits stipulated in Section 2 shall be computed as SIMPLE interest at the rate of 6% (six percent) per annum. No compounding of any kind shall apply.
3.2 The accrual period for interest under this Section 3 is stipulated at exactly 30 (thirty) months, running from the Breach Date to the agreed judgment reference date.
3.3 For the avoidance of doubt, interest under this Section 3 applies only to the Lost Profits in Section 2 and does not apply to the Consequential Carve-Out, which is governed exclusively by the separate Prejudgment Interest Terms Memorandum.

Section 4. Total Claim for Docketing Purposes.
4.1 The total stipulated claim on the lost-profits count equals the Lost Profits in Section 2 plus the prejudgment interest computed under Section 3, rounded to whole dollars.

Section 5. Consequential Carve-Out.
5.1 The Consequential Carve-Out comprises exactly two components: (a) lost resale margin on downstream contracts, stipulated at $512,000; and (b) incidental cover costs incurred in procuring substitute fabrication capacity, stipulated at $208,000.
5.2 Prejudgment interest on the Consequential Carve-Out is NOT set by this Schedule. It is governed exclusively by the Prejudgment Interest Terms Memorandum executed by the parties, which states the applicable rate and accrual period for the carve-out.

Section 6. Rounding; No Duplication.
6.1 All computed amounts shall be rounded to whole dollars. No component of damages may be counted more than once across Sections 2 through 5.

Executed by counsel of record for Meridian and Corvess.

HARLOW & TRENT LLP — FEE SCHEDULE AND Q2 BILLING SUMMARY

Client: Meridian Fabrication Corp.  |  Engagement: Corvess litigation (No. 24-cv-8812)
Billing Partner: Elena Voss  |  Period: April 1 – June 30 (Q2)

Part A. Governing Fee Schedule (per the executed engagement letter, Exhibit B).
A.1 Partner time (Elena Voss): $950 per hour.
A.2 Senior Associate time (Daniel Okafor): $520 per hour.
A.3 Paralegal time (Reyna Solis): $210 per hour.
A.4 Negotiated client discount: a discount of 10% (ten percent) applies to PROFESSIONAL FEES ONLY. The discount does not apply to disbursements or other charges.
A.5 Disbursements are billed at cost with no markup and no discount.

Part B. Q2 Recorded Hours (final, as approved by the billing partner after write-downs).
B.1 Partner (Voss): 120 hours.
B.2 Senior Associate (Okafor): 310 hours.
B.3 Paralegal (Solis): 85 hours.

Part C. Q2 Disbursements (at cost).
C.1 Aggregate disbursements for the period: $12,455. This figure comprises deposition transcripts, service of process, and travel, and is billed without markup pursuant to A.5.

Part D. Invoice Computation Method (per engagement letter Section 7).
D.1 Step 1 — compute gross professional fees: multiply each timekeeper's Q2 hours in Part B by that timekeeper's hourly rate in Part A, and sum the three products.
D.2 Step 2 — apply the 10% negotiated discount from A.4 to the gross professional fees from Step 1 (fees only).
D.3 Step 3 — add the aggregate disbursements in C.1 to the discounted fees from Step 2. The result, rounded to whole dollars, is the invoice amount for the quarter.
D.4 The discount is never applied to disbursements, and disbursements are never discounted, netted, or prorated.

Part E. Notes.
E.1 The hours in Part B are final; no additional write-downs or premiums apply to Q2.
E.2 Rates in Part A are unchanged from Q1 and remain in effect until Amendment No. 3, if any, is executed.
E.3 Questions regarding this summary should be directed to the billing partner.

Prepared by the Harlow & Trent LLP billing department for the quarterly true-up of the client invoice record.

DISCOVERY COST-SHARING STIPULATION AND VENDOR COST REPORT

Meridian Fabrication Corp. v. Corvess Industrial Group, LLC, No. 24-cv-8812 (D. Ariz.)

Pursuant to the Court's ESI Order, the parties submit this stipulation allocating the third-party vendor costs of the document production hosted by LitServe Data Solutions ("Vendor").

Section 1. Vendor Cost Components (invoiced to date, final for this allocation).
1.1 Processing. The Vendor processed 480 GB of collected data at the contracted rate of $75 per GB.
1.2 Hosting. The Vendor hosted the review database for 14 months at the contracted rate of $2,300 per month.
1.3 First-Pass Review Support. The Vendor's managed-review team performed first-pass review of 12,600 documents at the contracted per-document rate of $1.50 per document.
1.4 No other Vendor charges are subject to this stipulation. Aggregate Vendor cost means the sum of the amounts computed under 1.1, 1.2, and 1.3.

Section 2. Allocation.
2.1 The parties stipulate that the requesting party, Meridian, shall bear 60% (sixty percent) of the aggregate Vendor cost, and the producing party, Corvess, shall bear the remaining 40% (forty percent).
2.2 Meridian's allocated share shall be computed by multiplying the aggregate Vendor cost from Section 1.4 by 60%, rounded to whole dollars, and recorded on the discovery cost ledger for the matter.
2.3 The allocation in this Section 2 is a cost-shifting stipulation only and does not affect any party's right to seek taxation of costs at the conclusion of the action.

Section 3. Payment Mechanics.
3.1 The Vendor shall issue split invoices consistent with Section 2 beginning with the next billing cycle. Amounts already paid by either party shall be trued up against the allocated shares within 30 days.
3.2 Any dispute concerning the arithmetic of the allocation shall be resolved by reference to the contracted rates and volumes stated in Section 1, which the parties agree are accurate and complete.

Section 4. Reservation.
4.1 Nothing in this stipulation waives any objection to the merits, relevance, or admissibility of any produced document.

SO STIPULATED, by counsel of record for Meridian and Corvess, and approved by the Special Master for discovery.

LIQUIDATED DAMAGES NOTICE AND DELAY CERTIFICATION

Re: Corvess Plant Expansion Contract — Design-Build Agreement between Corvess Industrial Group, LLC ("Owner") and Talley Constructors, Inc. ("Contractor")

This Notice is issued by Owner pursuant to Section 11.4 of the Design-Build Agreement (the "Contract") and certifies the delay period for purposes of the liquidated damages assessment now tracked as a deadline-exposure item in the litigation file.

Section 1. Contractual Liquidated Damages Terms (quoted from Contract § 11.4).
1.1 Rate. "For each calendar day that Substantial Completion occurs after the Guaranteed Completion Date, Contractor shall pay Owner liquidated damages of $4,500 per calendar day."
1.2 Cap. "Contractor's aggregate liability for liquidated damages under this Section 11.4 shall not exceed $315,000, being seven percent (7%) of the original Contract Price of $4,500,000."
1.3 Exclusivity. Liquidated damages under § 11.4 are Owner's sole remedy for delay to Substantial Completion, and are subject to the cap in 1.2 in all circumstances.

Section 2. Delay Certification.
2.1 The Guaranteed Completion Date under the Contract was March 1.
2.2 Substantial Completion, as certified by the independent engineer, was achieved on May 15.
2.3 The parties' project representatives have jointly certified, and this Notice adopts, a delay period of exactly 75 (seventy-five) calendar days for purposes of the § 11.4 assessment. No excusable-delay credits remain outstanding; all time-extension requests have been resolved and are reflected in the certified 75-day figure.

Section 3. Assessment Method.
3.1 The assessed liquidated damages equal the certified delay period in 2.3 multiplied by the daily rate in 1.1, PROVIDED THAT if the product exceeds the cap stated in 1.2, the assessment is limited to the cap. The capped result, rounded to whole dollars, is the deadline exposure to be recorded.
3.2 Owner reserves all rights with respect to warranty claims and non-delay defaults, which are outside § 11.4 and outside the cap.

Section 4. Payment Demand.
4.1 Owner demands payment of the assessed amount within 30 days of this Notice. Failure to pay will result in a draw on the performance security in the amount of the assessment.

Issued by Owner's authorized representative, with a copy to the independent engineer and to counsel of record.

DISTRICT COURT FEE SCHEDULE AND FILING COST WORKSHEET

Meridian Fabrication Corp. v. Corvess Industrial Group, LLC — filing program for the District of Arizona action

This worksheet consolidates the court's published fee schedule with the firm's planned filings so that the total filing cost for the matter can be computed and recorded on the filings ledger.

Part A. Applicable Court Fee Schedule (as published by the Clerk).
A.1 Civil complaint filing fee: $402 (one filing required for this action).
A.2 Pro hac vice admission fee: $150 per admitted attorney.
A.3 Jury trial demand fee: $75 (one demand required for this action).

Part B. Planned Admissions.
B.1 Three (3) out-of-state attorneys will seek pro hac vice admission for this action: Elena Voss, Daniel Okafor, and appellate counsel Marta Reyes. Each admission incurs the per-attorney fee in A.2. No other admissions are planned.

Part C. Appeal Bond Premium.
C.1 In anticipation of post-judgment proceedings, the firm has bound a supersedeas bond in the penal amount of $210,000.
C.2 The surety's premium is 1.5% (one and one-half percent) of the bond amount for the annual term, payable once for the period covered by this worksheet.
C.3 The bond premium is a recorded filing-program cost for this matter and is included in the total filing cost computed under Part D.

Part D. Computation Method.
D.1 Total filing cost equals: the complaint filing fee (A.1), plus the pro hac vice fees for all planned admissions (A.2 multiplied by the number of attorneys in B.1), plus the jury demand fee (A.3), plus the bond premium computed under Part C. Round to whole dollars.
D.2 No other court costs (transcript fees, witness fees, copying) are included in this worksheet; those are tracked on the disbursement ledger, not the filings ledger.

Part E. Certification.
E.1 The rates and counts above were verified against the Clerk's current fee schedule and the surety's binder on the date of preparation. Any change in the number of admissions requires a revised worksheet before the ledger entry is made.

Prepared by the managing clerk's office, Harlow & Trent LLP.

PREJUDGMENT INTEREST TERMS MEMORANDUM — CONSEQUENTIAL CARVE-OUT

Meridian Fabrication Corp. v. Corvess Industrial Group, LLC, No. 24-cv-8812 (D. Ariz.)

This Memorandum is the instrument referenced in Section 5.2 of the parties' Stipulated Damages Schedule (Final Executed Copy). It states the exclusive prejudgment-interest terms for the Consequential Carve-Out defined in that Schedule. It does not restate the carve-out principal, which is fixed by the components stipulated in Section 5.1 of the Schedule.

Section 1. Scope.
1.1 This Memorandum governs prejudgment interest ONLY on the Consequential Carve-Out (lost resale margin and incidental cover costs, as stipulated in the Schedule). It has no application to the Lost Profits count, whose interest terms are fixed by Section 3 of the Schedule (simple interest at 6% per annum for a stipulated 30-month period).

Section 2. Rate and Method for the Consequential Carve-Out.
2.1 Rate. Prejudgment interest on the Consequential Carve-Out accrues at the statutory rate of 8% (eight percent) per annum.
2.2 Method. Interest is SIMPLE interest. No compounding, capitalization, or interest-on-interest applies.
2.3 Accrual Period. The accrual period is stipulated at exactly 21 (twenty-one) months.
2.4 Computation. Interest equals the carve-out principal (the sum of the two components stipulated in Section 5.1 of the Schedule) multiplied by the annual rate in 2.1, prorated for the accrual period in 2.3, with the result rounded to whole dollars.

Section 3. Docketing.
3.1 The total consequential exposure to be recorded on the docket equals the carve-out principal plus the interest computed under Section 2, rounded to whole dollars.
3.2 The docket entry shall not include any Lost Profits amount or any interest computed under Section 3 of the Schedule; the lost-profits count is docketed separately.

Section 4. Miscellaneous.
4.1 This Memorandum may be amended only in a writing signed by counsel of record for both parties.
4.2 In the event of any conflict between this Memorandum and any draft schedule or prior correspondence, this Memorandum controls as to consequential-carve-out interest.

Executed by counsel of record for Meridian and Corvess as of the date of the Final Executed Copy of the Stipulated Damages Schedule.

ENGAGEMENT BUDGET AMENDMENT NO. 2

Harlow & Trent LLP — Client: Meridian Fabrication Corp.
Engagement: Corvess Industrial litigation and related counseling

This Amendment No. 2 to the engagement letter dated January 9 (the "Engagement Letter") is entered into by the Firm and the Client to revise the approved fee budget for the matter. Capitalized terms not defined here have the meanings in the Engagement Letter.

Section 1. Background.
1.1 Under Amendment No. 1, the approved fee budget for the matter was set at $480,000 (four hundred eighty thousand dollars) (the "Original Approved Budget").
1.2 The matter has entered Phase 2 (expert discovery and dispositive motions), which the parties agree requires additional budget. Separately, the Firm has agreed to a one-time client-relations credit in connection with the Q1 invoicing delay.

Section 2. Budget Revision.
2.1 Phase 2 Increase. The approved fee budget is increased by an amount equal to 25% (twenty-five percent) of the Original Approved Budget stated in Section 1.1.
2.2 Client-Relations Credit. A one-time credit of $18,500 (eighteen thousand five hundred dollars) shall be SUBTRACTED from the budget in connection with the matters described in Section 1.2. The credit is applied once and does not recur.
2.3 Revised Budget Computation. The revised approved fee budget equals: the Original Approved Budget (Section 1.1), plus the Phase 2 Increase (Section 2.1), minus the Client-Relations Credit (Section 2.2), rounded to whole dollars. The revised figure is the new fee budget of record for the matter and shall be recorded on the matter's budget history.
2.4 The revised budget is a cap for planning purposes only and does not modify the fee schedule rates, which remain as stated in Exhibit B to the Engagement Letter.

Section 3. Effect.
3.1 Except as amended by this Amendment No. 2, the Engagement Letter and Amendment No. 1 remain in full force and effect.
3.2 This Amendment No. 2 supersedes any draft budget projections circulated by email, which were preliminary and are not to be recorded.

Agreed and accepted by the Firm's engagement partner and the Client's general counsel.

CORRESPONDENCE — MEDIATION FEE SPLIT AND SESSION LOGISTICS

From: Daniel Okafor, Harlow & Trent LLP
To: Counsel of record for Corvess Industrial Group, LLC
Re: Meridian v. Corvess — mediation before Hon. Patrice W. Camden (ret.)

Counsel:

Writing to confirm logistics and the fee split for the mediation session scheduled before Judge Camden (ret.) at the Camden ADR Center.

1. Mediator's fee. The mediator's engagement letter quotes a flat session fee of $14,000 for a full-day session, inclusive of preparation time up to eight hours. Consistent with the ADR Center's standard terms and our earlier call, the parties will split the mediator's fee evenly, 50/50, with each side remitting its half directly to the ADR Center within ten days of the session.

2. Room and administrative fee. The ADR Center charges a $600 facility and administration fee for the day. We propose the same even split. If your client prefers, we are equally content for each side to pay its own breakout-room incidentals and split only the main-room charge.

3. Position statements. Judge Camden requests confidential position statements not exceeding fifteen pages, due five business days before the session. Exhibits do not count against the page limit but should be tabbed.

4. Attendance. We will have our client's chief financial officer present with full settlement authority, along with lead trial counsel. Please confirm equivalent authority on your side, as the mediator's standing order requires principals with authority in the room.

5. No effect on ledgers. For clarity, mediation fees are handled by the clients directly under our respective engagement terms; nothing in this letter is to be recorded on the litigation cost ledgers, the filings ledger, or any damages computation in the case. This letter addresses logistics only and states no position on the merits or on any stipulated figure.

Please confirm by reply that the even split and the logistics above work for your side, and we will notify the ADR Center jointly.

Regards,
Daniel Okafor
Harlow & Trent LLP, counsel for Meridian Fabrication Corp.
